paper_title: Four-Terminal Tandem Based on a PM6:L8-BO Transparent Solar Cell and a 7 nm Ag Layer Intermediate Electrode
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Solar RRL - 2024 - Bernal‐Texca - Four‐Terminal Tandem Based on a PM6 L8‐BO Transparent Solar Cell and a 7 nm Ag Layer/auto/Solar RRL - 2024 - Bernal‐Texca - Four‐Terminal Tandem Based on a PM6 L8‐BO Transparent Solar Cell and a 7 nm Ag Layer.md

knowledge_points.content: The champion four-terminal tandem organic solar cell achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 16.94% using a PM6:L8-BO front cell and a PTB7-Th:O6T-4F back cell.
knowledge_points.evidence: The PCE of the champion four-terminal device was 16.94% exceeding the one from the best single-junction cell, for the PM6:L8-BO and PTB7-Th:O6T-4F as transparent front and filtered back cells, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: In a four-terminal (4T) tandem configuration, the subcells are electrically disconnected, which eliminates the current matching constraint required in two-terminal (2T) monolithic tandems.
knowledge_points.evidence: To overcome the shortcomings associated with the two-terminal tandems, an alternative is the four-terminal approach that consists of piling up a transparent cell with an opaque cell, being both cells electrically disconnected. In that configuration, current matching is no longer a constraint parameter.

knowledge_points.content: An ultrathin 7 nm Ag top electrode for the transparent front cell was fabricated using an ultrathin Au seed layer to promote a percolated surface and prevent island-like cluster formation on the MoO3 layer.
knowledge_points.evidence: In this work, we were able to fabricate a transparent electrode, as the last layer of the front cell, with a thickness of only 7 nm... To avoid this [island-like clusters], we deposited an ultrathin Au seed layer prior to the evaporation of the Ag contact.

knowledge_points.content: The 7 nm ultrathin Ag electrode exhibits a sheet resistance of approximately 18 Ω sq⁻¹, which is comparable to conventional ITO electrodes (15 Ω sq⁻¹).
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure 3b shows the sheet resistance as a function of the Ag thickness, which for the case of 7 nm, the value is ≈18 Ω sq⁻¹ A only slightly above of the sheet resistance from conventional ITO electrodes (15 Ω sq⁻¹).

knowledge_points.content: The PM6:L8-BO blend, with a bandgap of 1.425 eV, was selected as the optimal front cell material due to its reduced voltage loss (approximately 210 mV lower than PM6:ITIC-4F) and high fill factor (FF > 75%).
knowledge_points.evidence: In fact, as shown in Figure S3 of the SI, the voltage loss for the PM6:L8- BO blend is ≈210 mV smaller than the one for the PM6:ITIC-4F... This makes the PM6:L8-BO the optimal choice for the front cell.

knowledge_points.content: A dielectric multilayer structure consisting of WO3 (45 nm) / LiF (141 nm) / WO3 (52 nm) was integrated between the subcells to provide high transmission in the 750–1000 nm range and high reflectivity in the 500–700 nm range.
knowledge_points.evidence: Such a numerical approach... resulted in a configuration consisting of the thin Ag layer followed by a photonic multilayer composed of three dielectric layers alternating WO3 and LiF. ...the Ag-based electrode plus the WO3/LiF/WO3 structure exhibits a high transmission in the 750-1000 nm range and a high reflectivity in the 500-700 nm range.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis of the 6–8 nm Ag layers showed a root mean square roughness (Sq) of less than 1 nm, indicating high homogeneity and suppressed dewetting.
knowledge_points.evidence: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) images of the top electrode from Figure 3c-e show very good homogeneity with a root mean square roughness (Sq) of less than 1 nm, indicating a suppressed dewetting of the surface when growing Ag layer with thicknesses ranging from 6 to 8 nm.

knowledge_points.content: The transparent PM6:L8-BO front cell alone achieved a PCE of 12.02% (average) and 12.33% (champion), while the filtered PTB7-Th:O6T-4F back cell contributed a PCE of 4.61% (average) and 4.90% (champion).
knowledge_points.evidence: Table 2: PM6:L8-BO Transparent front cell PCE 12.02 ± 0.21 (12.33); Filtered back cell PCE 4.61 ± 0.23 (4.90).

knowledge_points.content: The transfer matrix formalism was employed to solve the inverse problem of finding the optimal optical performance for the front cell back electrode and the photonic multilayer.
knowledge_points.evidence: To find the optimal optical performance for the front cell, back electrode, and photonic multilayer, we used a standard inverse problem-solving approach combined with the transfer matrix formalism.

knowledge_points.content: The bandgaps of the materials used in this study are 1.746 eV for PM6:F-M, 1.600 eV for PM6:ITIC-4F, 1.425 eV for PM6:L8-BO, and 1.259 eV for PTB7-Th:O6T-4F.
knowledge_points.evidence: Table 1. Bandgapa) [eV]: PM6:F-M 1.746, PM6:ITIC-4F 1.600, PM6:L8-BO 1.425, PTB7-Th:O6T-4F 1.259.

knowledge_points.content: Both the transparent front cell and the opaque back cell utilized an inverted device structure: Glass/ITO/ZnO/Active Layer/MoO3/Ag.
knowledge_points.evidence: The four-terminal tandem construction started with the fabrication of the transparent front cells with the following inverted structure: Glass/ITO/ZnO/Active layer / MoO3 / Ag / WO3 / LiF / WO3. ...the back cell with the standard inverted structure Glass / ITO / ZnO / PTB7-Th:O6T-4F / MoO3 / Ag.
